reading.body:
Snowflake is primarily a data platform company with $4.7 billion in annual revenue, not an AI company, though it has added AI capabilities to its core infrastructure.

The company's position in the AI stack is as a compute and storage layer for data operations that support machine learning workloads. Snowflake Cortex embeds LLM functions, vector search, and governance into the data cloud itself, meaning AI models operate directly on data where it lives rather than requiring separate movement and infrastructure. Snowflake Arctic, an open-licensed LLM, serves as a reference model optimized for the data cloud environment. This architecture trades off independent AI compute specialization for integration with data engineering pipelines.

For AI scaling specifically, Snowflake's constraint is not whether it provides AI capability but whether consolidating AI inference and data processing in one platform reduces the total power and cooling footprint required to train and run models on large datasets. The data shows the company offers both infrastructure (the cloud platform itself) and software (the embedded AI functions), but does not show compute utilization, power consumption, or how much of Snowflake's $4.7 billion revenue comes from AI versus traditional analytics. Without those figures, the contribution of Snowflake's AI products to the broader compute and power demands of the AI ecosystem remains unclear.

profile_text.body:
Snowflake is a public company founded in 2012 and headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, USA. Its website describes an AI Data Cloud that supports AI, data engineering, applications, and analytics, and says the platform eliminates silos and accelerates innovation. The site also says Snowflake enables organizations to collaborate, build AI-powered data apps, and unlock data insights within a secure and scalable AI Data Cloud. It highlights Under Armour and Booking.com as customers using Snowflake for unified data, conversational AI, agentic workflows, and data modernization.

The company's AI products include Snowflake Arctic, an enterprise-focused LLM under an Apache 2.0 license with data cloud integration and commercial use, and Snowflake Cortex, which provides native AI in the data cloud with LLM functions, vector search, data residency controls, and governance via Snowflake Horizon.

Snowflake trades under the ticker SNOW and has CIK number 0001640147. Its most recent 10-K filing reports revenue of $4,683,946,000 for the period ended January 31, 2026. No Montana litigation is listed in the available facts.
